title: Mining and Analyzing Online Social Networks for Digital Peer Support
author: Rueger, Dolfsma, et al.

steps.title: Construct a social network
steps.instruction: Define the relationships within the online community to build the social network, where nodes typically represent users and edges represent the relationships between them (e.g., replies in a discussion forum).

substeps.instruction: Create an edge list where each row is a single edge, with the first column as the source node ID and the second column as the target node ID.
Alternatively, create an adjacency matrix where each row and column corresponds to a node, and cells represent edges using either dichotomous (0/1) or continuous (weighted) values.

steps.title: Perform social network analysis (SNA)
steps.instruction: Analyze the constructed network to understand the relationships between individuals and the roles they play within the larger group.

steps.title: Perform text and content analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the text posted in online communities to evaluate the purpose and implications of relationships, as well as users' views and opinions.

substeps.instruction: Evaluate objectivity, subjectivity, and personality of the text.
Use techniques such as sentiment analysis to focus on discussed topics and user feelings.

steps.title: Conduct longitudinal analysis
steps.instruction: Combine social network analysis and text analysis over time to examine how relationships and behavior co-evolve.
